pages.title: Pad-keepers
pages.text:
The Pad-keepers kept the hearths. Not the fires — the *warmth*: the banked heat in thin dirt that let a pad hold a family through a long dark.\
They were the first to notice the Loom was fraying, because the pads got cold before anything fell.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: Before the Cut they banked heat under whole continents: hearths under markets, under fields, under the first stair of every hanging city. What they lost was the long dark they had already solved — warmth as a public fact. Now they keep scraps, and they keep them anyway.

pages.title: Soil Strand
pages.text:
*We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm.*\
Seated. The Pad-keepers answer when this Post hums.

pages.title: Their camp
pages.text: The Pad-keepers keep a camp in the March steppe: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Earth totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: Their hearth favours dirt and moss blocks, bread, Echo Shards. Their Elder trades hearths and caches, and at Voice standing presses the tribe's Mark into your hand.
